= Haplogroup R-FTA30932: The Border Normans =


== General Information ==
* '''Haplogroup:''' R-FTA30932
* '''Parent Branch:''' [[R-FT4811]]
* '''Estimated TMRCA:''' c. 1100–1200 AD
* '''Primary Surnames:''' Chirnside (Churnside), Brown (Le Brun)
* '''Geography:''' Scottish Borders (Berwickshire), Virginia (USA), Jamaica.

== Biography ==
'''R-FTA30932''' represents a distinct lineage of Norse-Norman origin that settled in the '''Scottish Borders''' (specifically Berwickshire) during the 12th century.

Genetic analysis places this lineage as a "sibling" branch to the Derbyshire/Glasgow line (R-FT32941). Both lineages share a common ancestor in the immediate post-Conquest period (c. 1066–1100), representing a single Norman family unit that fractured into two distinct migratory paths:
# The '''Western Branch''' (R-FT32941) settled in Derbyshire (de Duffield) and later Lanarkshire (Glasgow).
# The '''Eastern Branch''' (R-FTA30932) settled in the Scottish Borders, becoming the families of '''Chirnside''' and '''Brown'''.

=== Historical Context: The Davidian Revolution ===
The proliferation of this haplogroup in Berwickshire is consistent with the "Davidian Revolution" (c. 1124–1153), where King David I invited Norman knights to settle the Scottish frontier to secure the border against England. Unlike their cousins who settled in the English Midlands, the progenitors of R-FTA30932 likely moved directly north into the Merse region of Scotland.

== Associated Surnames ==

=== Chirnside (de Chirnside) ===
This branch represents the '''territorial''' adoption of a surname. Upon receiving lands in the parish of Chirnside, Berwickshire, the Norman progenitor dropped his original family name and adopted the style ''de Chirnside'' (of Chirnside).
* '''Etymology:''' Territorial (Berwickshire).
* '''Key DNA Matches:''' Lineages tracing to '''Alexander Churnside''' (b. 1838, Jamaica). This suggests a branch of the Border family became involved in the colonial sugar trade in the Caribbean during the 18th or 19th centuries.

=== Brown (Le Brun / DeBrown) ===
This branch likely represents the "Anglicized Norman" descriptive surname ''Le Brun'' ("The Brown").
* '''Etymology:''' Descriptive / Norman.
* '''Norman Connection:''' The presence of the "Brown" surname within this specific, rare Norman haplogroup suggests these individuals descend from the noble house of '''Le Brun''' (Lords of Colstoun and patrons of the Borders), rather than unrelated English families of the same name.
* '''Key DNA Matches:''' Lineages tracing to '''Dixon Brown''' (b. 1758, Virginia). The use of the forename "Dixon" (a prominent Border Reiver surname) strongly indicates a Scottish Border origin prior to American emigration.

== Genetic Phylogeny ==
Current Big Y-700 testing has established the following hierarchy:
* '''R-M269'''
''' '''R-U106''' (Germanic/Nordic)
'''* '''R-FT4811''' (The Norman Patriarch, c. 1000 AD)
'''''' '''R-FTA30932''' (The Border Branch - Chirnside/Brown)
'''''' '''R-FT32941''' (The Derbyshire/Lanarkshire Branch - Duffield/Glasgow)

The split between FTA30932 and FT32941 marks the divergence of the family between the East Coast (Berwickshire) and the West/Midlands (Derbyshire/Glasgow) shortly after the Norman Conquest.

== Research Notes ==
* '''The "Uncle" Relationship:''' Testers positive for R-FTA30932 are not descendants of the Glasgow/Duffield line; they are genetic cousins. They share a common grandfather but descend from a parallel son who stayed in or moved to the Eastern Borders.
* '''Geographic Distribution:''' The concentration of this haplogroup in Berwickshire contrasts with the related R-FT32941, which is heavily concentrated in Lanarkshire and Derbyshire.
